newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore economic slowdown is cyclical - Hu.
newsitem.headline: Singapore economic slowdown is cyclical - Hu.

text.p: Singapore's economic slowdown is cyclical and does not reflect a deterioration in the city-state's external competitiveness, the chairman of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), Richard Hu, said in its 1996/97 annual report released on Tuesday.
Hu, who is also Finance Minister, said: "It is important to view this period of consolidation from a balanced perspective."
"The current slowdown has allowed the economy to take a breather following three to four years of above-trend growth. It has helped alleviate incipient overheating pressures."
The current slowdown appeared to be of "moderate severity" unlike previous cyclical downturns.
"Although the growth of GDP (gross domestic product) has declined well below the medium-term potential rate of seven percent per annum, the level of GDP is still close to potential," Hu said.
The downswing in the key manufacturing sector appeared to have bottomed out as suggested by the pick up in new orders for electronics goods in the U.S.
Singapore's real GDP grew by 4.6 percent during the second half of 1996 and by 3.8 percent in the first quarter of 1997.
This was sharply lower than the average of almost 10 percent per annum recorded in the preceding three-and-a-half years.
The MAS recognised the vulnerability of the economy to external shocks and this was reflected in its exchange rate policy.
"Developments in the external and domestic economic environment have allowed an easier exchange rate policy," he said.

Hu said he expected "a continuation of the current policy stance" as long as the global inflationary environment remained benign and domestic economic growth did not persistently exceed its underlying potential.
On asset inflation, Hu said the MAS had not been able to raise interest rates in an attempt to dampen asset inflation because its monetary policy was centred on the exchange rate.
Hence the government resorted to fiscal and prudential measures in May last year to curb excessive speculation in the property market, he said.
